gaps.sentence: This is the beach ___ we used to play as children.
gaps.explanation: 'Where' introduces place information; 'we used to play' already has a subject and object, so 'which' is impossible.

gaps.sentence: The 1990s was the decade ___ mobile phones became common.
gaps.explanation: 'When' replaces 'in which' after time nouns; 'which' cannot stand alone here.

gaps.sentence: I'll never forget the day ___ we first met.
gaps.explanation: 'When' replaces 'on which' after time nouns like day, year and moment.

gaps.sentence: The discussion got to a stage ___ nobody was listening any more.
gaps.explanation: 'A stage where ...' means 'a stage at which ...'; the clause has its own subject and verb, so 'which' is impossible.

gaps.sentence: Nobody knows the reason ___ he resigned so suddenly.
gaps.explanation: 'The reason why ...' is the standard pattern; 'why' means 'for which'.

gaps.sentence: Show me ___ you have written so far.
gaps.explanation: 'What you have written' means 'the things that you have written'; 'that' cannot head a nominal clause after 'me'.

gaps.sentence: The lawyers, against ___ the case was brought, denied everything.
gaps.hint: the case was brought against them
gaps.explanation: 'Against whom' is the formal relative pattern; 'who' and 'that' cannot follow prepositions.

gaps.sentence: He repaired the car ___ engine had failed.
gaps.hint: the engine belongs to the car
gaps.explanation: 'Whose engine' means 'the car's engine', showing possession even with objects.
